transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… well, I didn’t want to make too big a deal out of it, but I’ve been hearing voices. Like, clear voices, almost like someone is standing right there in my little studio. They’ll say my name, and say things like my work is being judged… even when it’s quiet and I know nobody else is there. I’m not trying to sound strange—I just thought I should come in and talk to someone.
When did you first start hearing these voices?

I guess… maybe around nine months ago? It wasn’t constant at first, so I tried to tell myself it was stress or just my imagination. But the voices, and the feeling that my work is being watched or judged, have been going on about that long. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had a period where you felt unusually energetic or wired for days at a time?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to call it a problem exactly, because sometimes I’m just trying to be productive. But there are times I get so much energy I can’t really sit down. I’ll clean my whole kitchen, start three different paintings, crochet half a blanket, and even rewrite care schedules all in the same night. It feels like I’m just… going and going. Is that what you mean?
During those high-energy times, do you need much less sleep than usual?

Yes… I guess I do. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve had a lot of nights where I only sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I get up feeling kind of charged, like I slept enough. Then I’ll just go right back to painting or start making calls and doing things. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you had a time during these past nine months when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not really sure… I mean, I’ve had down days, sure, but I don’t know if I’d say most of the day nearly every day. I try to keep moving and do what I’m supposed to do, so maybe I don’t notice it the same way. What would count as depressed, exactly?
During these past nine months, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voices even though you were not in one of those high-energy states?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but there was a stretch after that really energized feeling had kind of dropped off, and I was sleeping more like normal again… and the voices didn’t just stop.

They kept going for, I guess, several weeks. And I was still feeling like people were judging me or keeping track of how I was doing my work. I know that probably sounds bad, but that’s what it felt like.
Since the voices and the feeling of being judged first began, have they been present for at least six months in total?

Yes… I think so. It’s hard to say it like that, but since it first started, the voices and that feeling like people were watching or judging my work have been there off and on for about nine months now. I mean, not every single minute, but overall, yes… at least six months.
During those high-energy periods, did you feel unusually euphoric or excessively good?

Yeah… I guess I did. I don’t want to make it sound like I thought I was better than everybody, but there were times I felt really bright, like… chosen almost, like Greenville couldn’t hold all the plans I had in my head.

And then it could flip, too. I’d get irritated real fast over something small, like if a client asked me to repeat myself. I know that’s not good… but yes, it was more than just being in a good mood.
Over these past nine months, were those high-energy, less-sleep periods happening for a substantial part of the time?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was out of control the whole time, but for a lot of it I was either really wound up — making big plans, sleeping hardly at all, staying busy nonstop — or I was coming down from that but still not really back to myself.

So… yes, I’d say it was a pretty big part of the time. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms for about nine months, including auditory hallucinations and persecutory/judgment-related delusional ideas, along with clear manic symptoms such as elevated/irritable mood, markedly increased energy, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, and expansive/grandiose thinking. Psychotic symptoms also persisted for several weeks outside a high-energy mood episode, and manic symptoms were present for a substantial portion of the illness. This pattern is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, manic type.
